notification_reason: A significant new Point Clear sensing fault and a material NGOFS2 guidance reversal meet the alert policy. Two of three Point Clear owner cameras failed the current cycle, and the six-hour model window reversed from strongly shoreward to seaward. No Jubilee is confirmed.
principal_dawn_visual_assessment_status: COMPLETED. The first after-dawn owner burst at 06:10–06:14 CDT had limited Point Clear detectability, so the principal call uses the first published dawn+20 follow-up at 06:31–06:34 CDT. All six cameras were healthy with valid three-frame bursts; five had moderate and montrose_pier_bird high detectability; no Jubilee, searching, flashlight or collecting signal was resolved. Post-dawn public live-player checks at 06:36–06:37 CDT were probably fresh and yielded scoped no-event evidence in their visible areas.

active_faults.impact: Point Clear owner-camera coverage reduced to 1/3; failed inputs remain UNKNOWN. Two consecutive all-six healthy cycles are required to close the fault.

known_unknowns: No current Point Clear/Daphne bottom dissolved-oxygen profile or nearshore_contact_strip_DO measurement is available.
Observed nearshore current and observed Point Clear water level are unavailable; NGOFS2 is model guidance only.
USGS Bucks tidally filtered discharge remains stale through September 4; tide-affected raw flow is not a direct freshwater-load measure.
Coffeeville current numerical discharge/timestamp was not defensibly recovered; Claiborne is stale for live scoring.
Point Clear close beach/swash and both Fairhope beaches remain outside validated public views; Fairhope also does not show Fly Creek.
Exact capture time and total upstream delay for both probably-fresh public live sessions remain unknown.
change_summary: The 23:07–23:10 CDT owner-camera cycle introduced a significant Point Clear fault: `pcl_e2_back_deck` and `pcl_e3_bay_mouth` failed, leaving 1/3 Point Clear owner cameras operational. The four surviving cameras produced coherent 3-frame bursts; nighttime biological detectability was low except one moderate Montrose view, so most biology remains UNKNOWN. Fresh NGOFS2 03Z guidance changed from approximately +44/+162/+237/−119 m to +62/+75/−109/−304 m at 1/3/6/12 hours, reversing the six-hour window seaward and strengthening twelve-hour seaward transport. Grand Hotel and Fairhope live players advanced across isolated 34.662- and 34.661-second samples at 23:48 CDT; Fairhope was already in its disabled currently-playing-live state. No searching, flashlights or collecting appeared, and water biology remained UNKNOWN in darkness. KBFM was calm and clear at 22:53 CDT. No independently dated September 13 Jubilee report surfaced.
